nearby_not_selected.name: Count Entity Instances by Acquisition Events
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a question asks how many of a category an entity has or owns as of a target date and no direct summary count is found.
content: When asked for a count of items an entity has as of a target date, search for individual membership-changing events (adoption, purchase, acquisition, birth, receipt, loss, sale) using structured queries with the entity and memory_kinds=['event'], plus keywords like 'adopted', 'bought', 'got', 'welcomed', 'acquired', 'sold', or 'gave away'.
Enumerate distinct instances whose event world_start is on or before the target date and whose world_end, if any, is after the target date; count those instances.

Do not count plans, considerations, or intentions to acquire as current possessions. If a retrieved memory mentions a plan or a named companion, inspect related memories to verify whether the acquisition already occurred before answering.
Stop after retrieving all candidate instances or after one additional targeted search that returns no new acquisition events; avoid exhaustive expansion.

nearby_not_selected.name: Duration questions search profile and state memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks how long a person has had, owned, or possessed something (e.g., 'how long has X had Y?'), search profile and state memories as well as event memories.
content: When a question asks how long a subject has had, owned, or possessed an item (e.g., 'how long has Nate had his turtles?'), interpret it as asking for a duration, not a specific acquisition date.
Do not restrict the search to event memories for such duration/tenure questions; include profile and state memory kinds because ownership duration is commonly stored as a profile or state fact.
If a profile or state memory directly states the duration, stop searching and answer with that duration; do not substitute a recent event date.

nearby_not_selected.name: Temporal filter for post-event activity queries
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks how someone spends time after a major life event, first find the event date and run searches limited to memories at or after that date, including planned future activities.
content: If the question references a life event (wedding, marriage, graduation, move, new job) and a later period (after, since, post-), locate that event's date from memory before answering.
Run hybrid/structured searches for the person's activities with a time filter: world_start on or after the event date; include planned future events and activity/event memory kinds.
If top results are dated before the event or do not fit the post-event window, add event-specific keywords (e.g., honeymoon, celebration) and re-search; do not answer from pre-event memories.
Stop once a coherent set of post-event activities covering the question's claims is retrieved; do not keep expanding after that.

nearby_not_selected.name: Date-consistent evidence selection
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question specifies a particular date, use only memories that were valid at that date, discard later memories, and re-search without a time filter if the initial search is inconclusive.
content: When the user question contains a specific date, treat it as a hard temporal constraint: consider only memories with world_start <= date and (world_end is null or world_end >= date).

If the initial date-constrained search does not yield sufficient evidence, run one additional hybrid search with time_mode='none' to surface all candidate memories, then filter the results to the target date before judging sufficiency.

When multiple candidate facts could answer the question, prefer the memory whose world_start is closest to and not after the question date; discard memories from after that date even if they are more semantically similar.

nearby_not_selected.name: Origin retrieval background first
nearby_not_selected.description: When a question asks how or when someone started, was introduced to, or first experienced an activity, use this Skill to restore missing origin evidence.
content: If the question targets the origin/start of an activity (e.g., 'how did X get introduced to', 'when did X start', 'first time'), run an extra hybrid/BM25 search with origin phrases: 'X started [activity]', 'X first [activity]', 'since childhood', 'introduced by', 'family/father/mother'.

When reviewing retrieved memories, prefer biographical sentences that mention when or how the activity began (e.g., 'since childhood', 'started with', 'watched with') even if stored inside preference/state memories; do not rely only on recent event memories.
Stop after 2-3 targeted origin searches; if no origin evidence appears, answer from the best available current evidence.
